question: Do the default stores survive a double fault (crash during recovery) and an fsync EIO without losing an acknowledged write?
flips_if: SQLite FULL fails -> redb default (or vice versa)

measured.harness: oracles/crash-harness (LD_PRELOAD tracer, persistence-model image enumeration), laptop i7 Legion 5, 2026-10-25
measured.sqlite_wal_full: 0 lost acks across main, EIO and double-fault stages (SQLite 3.53.2 via rusqlite 0.40.2 bundled)
measured.redb_2pc: 0 lost acks with the bootstrap parent-directory fsync; 111/780 images lose acks without it
measured.controls: WAL+NORMAL loses acks in 624/790 images; ack-before-fsync 680/800; EIO-as-success caught at all 4 positions
measured.new_failure_mode: if the first fsync fails during WAL conversion, SQLite silently falls back to rollback-journal mode although PRAGMA journal_mode returned 'wal'; acked writes are then lost unless the store re-reads journal_mode/synchronous after the first write and refuses to serve

decision_effect: SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL single writer stays the default store; redb 2PC stays the pure-Rust option. New mandatory aegis-state startup assertions: (1) after the first committed write, re-read PRAGMA journal_mode = 'wal' and synchronous = 2 (FULL), else refuse to serve; (2) create store files via temp file + rename + parent-directory fsync; (3) fsync the parent directory at bootstrap before serving; (4) any fsync error is fatal for the store (no retry-then-ack).
rung: R1 executed (measurement grade A for the model; one host, reduced image count)
reproduce: oracles/crash-harness/run ; oracles/crash-harness/run --self-test ; full size: HEAVY_TIMEOUT=7200 oracles/crash-harness/run --full --jobs 16
limits: Reduced image count (19,860 of ~170k full); one EIO per run; double fault one level deep; raw syscalls/io_uring bypass the tracer (Rust subjects need --cfg rustix_use_libc); persistence model is ext4-like, other filesystems not covered.
